Ostensible

os-TEN-suh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ostensible is stated or appearing to be true, but not necessarily so; put forward as the reason, though perhaps not the real one.

The store's ostensible closing time was 9 p.m., but the manager quietly let regular customers keep shopping well past ten.

Worked Example

When the celebrity chef closed her flagship restaurant, citing 'creative burnout' in a brief press release, insiders later revealed a far messier financial dispute with her business partner lurking behind that ostensible explanation.

Ostensible marks a stated reason or appearance that's presented to the world, while hinting that the real truth might be something else entirely.

How Ostensible Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

apparent

apparent: seeming to be true based on what is visible or stated

professed

professed: openly declared, though not necessarily sincere

Antonyms

genuine

genuine: real and true, without pretense

actual

actual: existing in fact, not merely claimed

How Strong Is It? — claimed → ostensible → deceptive

claimed vs. ostensible

claimed vs. ostensible: Claimed just reports what someone said, without necessarily hinting that it's false.

deceptive vs. ostensible

deceptive vs. ostensible: Deceptive goes further than ostensible -- it means the false front was built on purpose, to intentionally mislead.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of ostensible.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — os-

Prefix — os-: toward, in front of (Latin ob-, which becomes os- before t)

Root — tens

Root — tens: to stretch, to show, to hold out (from Latin tendere, 'to stretch,' whose past-participle stem is tens-)

Suffix — -ible

Suffix — -ible: able to be (Latin -ibilis)

Put it together

Put it together: Ostensible comes from os- ('toward,' the form Latin ob- takes before t) + tens ('to stretch, to show,' from Latin tendere) + -ible -- together Latin ostendere, 'to show, display.' The same tend-/tens- root shows up in pretend -- literally 'to stretch forth' a claim. An ostensible reason is one 'held out' for display, whether or not it's the whole truth.

Use the root in a new word: pretend

Use the root in a new word: pretend: The children decided to pretend the living room floor was made entirely of lava.

Word Choice

Ostensible almost always signals a gap between what's claimed and what's really going on -- reach for it whenever you want to describe a stated reason while hinting the real one might be different.
